subject: Cloud Computing
title: Sovereign Clouds and Data Nationalism
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Sovereign Clouds and Data Nationalism.

hook.text: Countries are demanding that their citizens' data stays within their borders. Sovereign clouds are the answer.

buildup.text: GDPR in Europe, data localization laws in India and China — governments want control over where data physically resides.

discovery.text: Cloud providers are building sovereign regions: isolated infrastructure operated by local partners under local laws.

twist.text: Sovereign clouds fragment the global internet. What was one seamless cloud becomes a patchwork of national boundaries.

climax.text: Global innovation versus national sovereignty — that tension is reshaping how cloud providers build their services.

punchline.text: Your data must stay in your country. The cloud obeys borders now.

quiz.question: What drives the demand for sovereign clouds?
options: Data localization laws that require citizens' data to stay within national borders
Cloud providers wanting to charge more for regional services
Technical limitations that prevent data from crossing borders

details.summary: Sovereign clouds operate under the legal jurisdiction of a specific nation, ensuring data and operations are fully governed by local laws. Driven by GDPR, geopolitical tensions, and data nationalism, countries are building or requiring sovereign cloud options independent of US tech companies.
details.whyItMatters: Sovereign clouds fragment the global cloud market along national boundaries. They create both opportunities for local providers and compliance challenges for global organizations.
takeaways: Sovereign clouds operate under a single nation's legal jurisdiction
GDPR and geopolitical tensions accelerate sovereignty demands
Major providers partner with local firms to offer sovereign options

faq.question: Why do countries want sovereign clouds?
faq.answer: The US CLOUD Act allows American authorities to access data held by US companies anywhere in the world. Countries want assurance that their data is not subject to foreign government access. Sovereign clouds ensure data, operations, and access remain under local legal jurisdiction.

faq.question: How do hyperscalers offer sovereign options?
faq.answer: AWS, Azure, and Google partner with local companies who operate the infrastructure under local jurisdiction. Google partnered with T-Systems in Germany and Thales in France. Microsoft partnered with SAP for EU data boundary commitments.
